Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (Nexa_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short SOC 2 summary to start the compliance thread. I wanted to surface a concise staging/acceptance checklist so we can align the MAP's gating criteria before the pilot. High level asks:

- Decision goal: choose deployment mode for pilot (Hosted) and evaluation gate for dedicated/private for 12-month roadmap.
- Staging acceptance criteria (recommended):
  - Functional: model responses pass 90% of the provided eval prompts (same prompt set used across modes).
  - Latency: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn text gen at 50 QPS (simulated 1k concurrent users, average seq len 256).
  - Stability: no more than 3 transient errors per 10k requests over a 24h run.
  - Cost threshold: total inference cost delta for pilot does not exceed 40% vs hosted baseline per 1M tokens.
  - Data residency: EU data pinned to eu-west region for evaluation (if EU dataset included).

- Security artifacts requested up front: SOC 2 summary (attached), encryption-in-transit + at-rest plan, KMS/HSM options, and audit log sample.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) Week 0: MAP sign-off + NDAs/PO prep
2) Week 1-2: Pilot (Hosted, us-east) — runs eval prompts + load test
3) Week 3: Gate review (results + go/no-go on Dedicated eval in eu-west)
4) Week 4-6: Dedicated evaluation (if required) + procurement pricing finalize
5) Week 8: Final decision and roll plan (Hosted commit or Dedicated contract)

Attached files: Nexa_MAP_v1.xlsx, SOC2_summary.pdf, latency-bench-50qps.csv (bench harness output).

Can you confirm the MAP milestones look achievable from your side and call out any hard constraints (procurement windows, legal review dates, or required on-site security review)? We can update the MAP and return a pricing appendix for hosted vs dedicated vs private.

Best,
Ben

Ben / Rishi / Sarah — ran the bench and updated the MAP draft (attached Nexa_MAP_v1.1.xlsx). Summary of findings and recommended MAP adjustments below.

Bench highlights (same model config, quantized FP16 path):
- us-east (hosted, standard node): p95 = 138ms at sustained 50 QPS, average first-token cold start = 220ms
- eu-west (hosted equivalent): p95 = 165ms at sustained 50 QPS (network delta + infra differences)
- Under a dedicated pool (4x GPU pool, pinned), p95 = 120ms at 50 QPS in eu-west (no cross-region egress).
- Error rate during 24h steady-run: 0.6 per 10k requests (within staging target).

Recommendations:
1) Pilot approach: run a 2-week Hosted pilot in us-east for non-PHI traffic starting Aug 16. During the pilot, route EU PHI dataset to a eu-west dedicated eval (short-lived nodes) to preserve residency for sensitive data. This hybrid pilot satisfies both speed to value and residency constraints.

2) MAP timeline (updated):
  - Week of Aug 16: Hosted pilot (us-east) + eu-west dedicated eval for PHI (two-track)
  - Week of Aug 30: Gate review — evaluate latency, eval prompt pass-rate, cost delta; produce executive one-pager for Nexa procurement
  - Sept 6–30: If go-ahead, procurement & contract negotiation for Dedicated (or Private)

3) Acceptance tweaks: bump EU gating p95 target to 170ms for hosted eu-west to account for observed network delta; dedicated evaluation target remains p95 <= 140ms. Keep functional eval pass-rate unchanged (>=90%).

Next steps I can own: attach bench CSV and a one-page bench summary to updated MAP; I will also attach the KMS keyflow diagram from infra. Rishi, can you share pricing appendix by Wed Aug 12 so Sarah has budget numbers before the pilot? Ben, if Nexa confirms the pilot week of Aug 16 we will finalize the small SOW for the dedicated eval nodes.

Sarah / Tom — please reply with a quick sign-off on the two-track pilot (hosted us-east for non-PHI + eu-west dedicated eval for PHI). If we get sign-off we will lock dates and runbooks.

Thanks,
